mainTopic: גנב vs. גזלן and the ארבעה וחמשה payments; the משנה on animals one may not raise
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: a rental that comes with a שטר must be a rental of land, since movables are not acquired with a document. Next comes רבי אלעזר's ruling that a thief who hid in the woods and then slaughtered or sold an animal pays ארבעה וחמשה. The גמרא explains that he moved the animal with a stick, and that because he was hiding, he counts as a גנב even though people saw him. רבי אבהו and רבי יוחנן then each give an example of a real גזלן: בניהו בן יהוידע, or the בעלי שכם who robbed from ambush. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains that the Torah is stricter with a גנב because he fears people more than הקב״ה, and a parable of two feasts supports this. Two sages then give reasons why an ox pays five and a sheep pays four. A new משנה lists animals that may not be raised: small animals in settled parts of ארץ ישראל, chickens in ירושלים or by כהנים, pigs anywhere, unchained dogs, and pigeon traps near settled areas. The גמרא brings ברייתות that explain where small animals are allowed, why large animals were never banned, and the short thirty-day allowance before a רגל.

steps.title: Movables are not acquired with a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the rental under discussion could involve a שטר if it were a rental of movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this is talking about renting movable things, are movables the kind of thing you write a document for?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the way the earlier source was understood. That source spoke of a rental together with a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items are acquired by physical acts, such as pulling them. They are not acquired by writing a שטר. So if the case involved a document, it cannot be a rental of movables.

keyTerms.meaning: subject to (acquired by) a written document

steps.confusionAlert: This line closes a discussion that began before this section. It is not the start of a new topic.

phrases.english: A rental of movable property?
Is movable property subject to a deed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִטַּלְטְלִי בְּנֵי שְׁטָרָא נִינְהוּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the rental in the earlier source was of movables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שטר does not apply to movables, so the case cannot be a movables rental.

steps.title: It is a rental of land
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the case is a rental of land, which can involve a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is talking about renting land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא solves the problem by changing what kind of rental the case is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land can be transferred or rented with a שטר. Once the case is moved from movables to land, the mention of a document fits.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A rental of land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (land instead of movables)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rental was of movables, which makes a document impossible
steps.terutzMaskana: The rental was of land, where a document works

steps.title: A hidden thief who slaughters or sells pays four or five times
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that someone seen hiding in the woods who then slaughtered or sold an animal pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: if people saw him hide in the woods, and he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays the four-or-five-times payment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי אלעזר gives a ruling about a thief who hid near the animals and then slaughtered or sold one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine of ארבעה וחמשה applies only to a גנב who steals an animal and then slaughters or sells it. רבי אלעזר holds that this hiding person fits that category. Steps 4 and 6 will question this.

keyTerms.meaning: the fourfold or fivefold payment of a thief (for a sheep or an ox)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
If they saw him hiding in the woods
and he slaughtered or sold,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief seen hiding in the woods who slaughtered or sold an animal pays ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: But he never pulled the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the thief never acquired the animal by pulling it, so how can he owe ארבעה וחמשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should he pay? He never pulled the animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person only counts as a thief once he takes possession, normally by משיכה (pulling). Here it sounds like he came out and slaughtered the animal where it stood. Without a theft, there can be no ארבעה וחמשה.

keyTerms.meaning: pulled (the act that acquires an animal)

phrases.english: Why?
But he did not pull it!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling of ארבעה וחמשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No pulling means no acquisition, and no acquisition means no theft that could bring the fine.

steps.title: He drove it with a stick
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the thief hit the animal with a stick so that it moved, and that counts as taking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is a case where he struck it with a stick.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by describing the case more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting the animal so that it walks moves it, and that counts like pulling. So the theft is complete before the slaughter or sale, and the fine applies.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Where he struck it with a stick.
phrases.notes: Hitting the animal makes it walk, and that movement works like pulling it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case so that an act of acquisition happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He slaughtered the animal without moving it, so there was no theft
steps.terutzMaskana: He moved it with a stick, which acquires it

steps.title: If people saw him, isn't he a robber?
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis object that since he was seen, he should be a גזלן (robber), and a גזלן does not pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: but since people saw him, he is a robber!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge is raised against רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גנב takes things secretly, while a גזלן takes things openly. ארבעה וחמשה applies only to a גנב. Since people watched him, it seems he acted openly, which would make him a גזלן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up גנב and גזלן. A גנב steals secretly and pays double, or four or five times. A גזלן takes openly and only returns what he took.

phrases.english: They said:
But since they saw him,
he is a robber!

steps.kashyaTarget: Calling the hidden person a גנב in רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being seen makes the act open, which would make him a גזלן who is not subject to ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Hiding from people makes him a thief
steps.stepSummary: Since he was trying to hide from the people, he counts as a גנב even though they saw him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he was hiding from them, he is a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that what decides the matter is how the thief behaves, not whether someone happened to see him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גנב is defined by trying to act in secret. This person hid from the people, so he was trying to sneak. That makes him a גנב, even though they noticed him.
steps.whatToRemember: A גנב is someone who tries to act in secret, even if he is seen. Because of this, רבי אלעזר's hiding thief pays ארבעה וחמשה.

phrases.english: Since he was hiding from them,
he is a thief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the category by the person's intent to hide
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being seen makes him a גזלן
steps.terutzMaskana: Trying to hide makes him a גנב, even if he is seen

steps.title: Then what is a robber?
steps.stepSummary: If even someone who is seen can be a גנב, the גמרא asks what case counts as a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does a robber look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear example of a גזלן, now that being seen is not enough. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer took away the simple idea that 'seen' means 'robber.' So the גמרא needs a new definition of a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what does it look like?

phrases.english: But then, what is the case of a robber?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא גַּזְלָן הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition or example of a true גזלן

steps.title: A robber is like בניהו בן יהוידע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says a גזלן is someone who openly takes by force, like בניהו בן יהוידע, who grabbed the spear from the Egyptian.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: like בניהו בן יהוידע, as it says, 'He robbed the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers with an example from תנ"ך of taking something openly, by force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בניהו did not hide at all. He grabbed the spear right out of the Egyptian's hand. The פסוק calls this ויגזול, robbery. So a גזלן takes openly and by force, while someone who hides is a גנב.
steps.whatToRemember: A גזלן takes openly and by force, like בניהו grabbing the spear. A גנב tries to sneak, even if people see him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Like Benaiah ben Jehoiada,
as it is stated:
"And he robbed the spear from the Egyptian's hand,
and killed him with his own spear."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזלן is someone who takes openly and by force, as shown by בניהו בן יהוידע and the פסוק's word ויגזול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line between גנב and גזלן, and that line decides who pays the extra fines of כפל and ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's example: the בעלי שכם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different example of a גזלן: the בעלי שכם, who robbed travelers from ambush.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A robber is like the men of Shechem, as the verse says: "The men of Shechem set ambushers on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the same question from Step 8 ("what is a גזלן?"), but he gives a different example than רבי אבהו did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's example was בניהו בן יהוידע, who took the spear openly by force. רבי יוחנן points to the בעלי שכם, whom the פסוק also describes with the word "וַיִּגְזְלוּ" (they robbed), even though they waited in ambush. The next steps discuss whether their hiding matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The men (leaders) of the city of Shechem
And they robbed (the word for גזילה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like the men of Shechem,
as it is stated: "And the men of Shechem set for him
ambushers on the tops of the mountains,
and they robbed all that
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: passed by them on the road."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן בַּעֲלֵי שְׁכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of Step 8, alongside רבי אבהו's answer in Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזלן is like the בעלי שכם, who robbed travelers from ambush.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אבהו use the example of the בעלי שכם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אבהו did not bring the בעלי שכם as his example.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו: why didn't he bring his example from this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step: why didn't רבי אבהו also bring the example of the בעלי שכם, like רבי יוחנן did?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the בעלי שכם also calls their act גזל, just like the פסוק about בניהו. So the גמרא wants to know what bothered רבי אבהו about this example. The answer in Step 12 is that they were hiding.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abahu: what is the reason
that he did not say it from this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי אבהו's example (Step 9) with רבי יוחנן's (Step 10).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אבהו avoided the example of the בעלי שכם.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: people who hide are not robbers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו would say that since the בעלי שכם were hiding, they are not true גזלנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: since they were hiding, they are not robbers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אבהו. Because the בעלי שכם hid in ambush, he does not see them as true גזלנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits Step 7: someone who hides from people counts as a גנב, not a גזלן. For רבי אבהו, a real גזלן takes openly with no hiding at all, like בניהו.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Since they were hiding,
they are not robbers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: כֵּיוָן דְּמִטַּמְּרִי אִיטַּמּוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 on behalf of רבי אבהו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hiding makes someone a גנב, so the בעלי שכם are not a clean example of a גזלן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they hid only so travelers wouldn't run away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the בעלי שכם hid only so travelers would not see them and flee, not because they were afraid to rob in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן? The fact that they were hiding was so that people would not see them and run away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן would respond to רבי אבהו's point. The hiding was only a trap to catch travelers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גנב hides because he is afraid of being seen while taking. The בעלי שכם were not afraid. They hid only so their victims wouldn't escape, and then they robbed them openly. So for רבי יוחנן they are still true גזלנים.
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is WHY someone hides. Hiding out of fear of being seen while taking makes a גנב. Hiding only to set a trap, and then taking openly by force, can still be a גזלן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan?
This, that they were hiding,
was so that people would not see them
and run away from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן – הָא דְּקָא מִטַּמְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יוחנן's example against the reasoning given for רבי אבהו in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the hiding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בעלי שכם hid, they should count as גנבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: They hid only to trap their victims, not out of fear of being seen taking, so they are גזלנים.

steps.title: Why is the Torah stricter with a thief than a robber?
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ask why a גנב is punished more than a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: Why was the Torah stricter with a thief than with a robber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new section of אגדה, a teaching about the meaning behind the law. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a גנב pays כפל and ארבעה וחמשה. A גזלן just returns what he took. That seems backwards, because a גזלן who takes by force seems worse.

keyTerms.meaning: A thief, who takes in secret

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the Torah is stricter with the גזלן because he uses force. The extra payments of כפל and ארבעה וחמשה apply only to the גנב.

phrases.english: His students asked
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai:
For what reason was the Torah stricter
with a thief more than with a robber?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic discussion, building on the difference between גנב and גזלן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the Torah fines a גנב more heavily than a גזלן.

steps.title: The thief fears people more than God
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains that the גזלן treats people and הקב״ה the same, but the גנב gives people more respect than הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This one (the robber) treated the honor of the servant the same as the honor of his Master. And that one (the thief) did not treat the honor of the servant the same as the honor of his Master.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers his students. The difference is about whom each one is afraid of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזלן is not afraid of people or of הקב״ה, so at least he treats them equally. The גנב hides from people but not from הקב״ה. That means he shows more respect to the "servant" (people) than to the "Master" (הקב״ה), and so he is punished more.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a money law into a lesson about יראת שמים. Hiding a sin from people while ignoring הקב״ה is a deeper failing.

phrases.english: He said to them:
This one equated the honor of the servant
phrases.notes: "This one" is the robber, who isn't afraid of anyone.

phrases.english: to the honor of his Master,
and that one did not equate the honor of the servant
to the honor of his Master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: זֶה – הִשְׁוָה כְּבוֹד עֶבֶד לִכְבוֹד קוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גנב fears people but not הקב״ה, so he is punished more.

steps.title: The thief acts as if God doesn't see or hear
steps.stepSummary: The גנב behaves as if ה׳'s eye cannot see and ה׳'s ear cannot hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it were, he treats the Eye "below" as if it doesn't see, and the Ear "below" as if it doesn't hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains more sharply what the גנב is really doing. This sets up the פסוקים that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By hiding only from people, the גנב acts as though ה׳ is not watching. The word כביכול ("as it were") warns us that this is only a way of speaking about ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: As it were, a way of speaking about ה׳ with respect
Below (a respectful way of speaking about ה׳)

phrases.english: As it were, he made the eye below
phrases.notes: "Below" is a respectful way of speaking. It really means ה׳'s eye, but the גמרא avoids saying it directly.

phrases.english: as if it does not see,
and the ear below
as if it does not hear,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּבְיָכוֹל עָשָׂה עַיִן שֶׁל מַטָּה כְּאִילּוּ אֵינָהּ רוֹאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the answer in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גנב acts as if ה׳ does not see or hear.

steps.title: Three verses about people who think God doesn't see
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings three פסוקים that describe people who imagine ה׳ does not see what they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Woe to those who go deep to hide their plans from ה׳, and their deeds are in the dark." And it says: "They say: ה׳ will not see, and the God of יעקב will not understand." And it says: "For they said: ה׳ has left the land, and ה׳ does not see."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the idea from Step 16 with three פסוקים. The next step adds a parable that backs up the same explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three פסוקים describe the same mistake: sinning in secret because you think ה׳ is not watching. This is exactly the attitude of the גנב.
steps.whatToRemember: A גנב pays more than a גזלן because he hides from people but not from הקב״ה. He acts as if ה׳ doesn't see, just like the people described in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Woe to those who go deep from ה׳
to hide their plans,
and their deeds are in the dark, etc."
And it is written: "And they say: ה׳ will not see,
and the God of Yaakov will not understand."
And it is written: "For they said: ה׳ has left the land,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 9:9. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and ה׳ does not see."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִים מֵה׳ לַסְתִּר עֵצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings פסוקים to support the idea in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the גנב acts as if ה׳ does not see

steps.title: The parable of the two feasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר brings a parable in the name of רבן גמליאל. It supports רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's idea that the גנב is worse because he shows people more respect than he shows הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר said: They told a parable in the name of רבן גמליאל. What is this like? Two people in the same city each made a feast. One invited the townspeople but did not invite the king's sons. The other invited neither the townspeople nor the king's sons. Which one deserves the bigger punishment? Clearly, the one who invited the townspeople but not the king's sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parable that backs up what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said in the previous steps: the גנב is punished more than the גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ignoring everyone is bad. But inviting the townspeople and leaving out the king's sons is an open insult to the king. In the same way, the גזלן ignores both people and הקב״ה, while the גנב hides from people and does not care about הקב״ה, so his insult to הקב״ה is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say / the answer is clearly

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which guest list matches which person. The one who invited the townspeople and left out the king's sons is like the גנב, and he is the one punished more.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir said:
They told a parable in the name of Rabban Gamliel:
What is this matter like?
It is like two people who lived in a city
and each made a feast.
One invited the people of the city
phrases.notes: This one matches the גנב: he cares how people see him, but not how הקב״ה sees him.

phrases.english: but did not invite the king's sons.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לֹא זִימֵּן אֶת בְּנֵי הָעִיר
phrases.english: And the other did not invite the people of the city
phrases.notes: This one matches the גזלן, who treats people and הקב״ה the same.

phrases.english: and did not invite the king's sons either.
Which of them deserves a greater punishment?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה שֶׁזִּימֵּן אֶת בְּנֵי הָעִיר
phrases.english: You must say: the one who invited the people of the city
but did not invite the king's sons.

steps.whatToRemember: The גנב is worse than the גזלן because he shows people more respect than he shows הקב״ה, just like the host who invited the townspeople but left out the king's sons.
steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מָשְׁלוּ מָשָׁל מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parable that illustrates and supports the explanation of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a גנב is punished more than a גזלן because he respects people more than הקב״ה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable from a ברייתא, told by רבי מאיר in the name of רבן גמליאל

steps.title: An ox pays five because work matters
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that a stolen ox brings a five-fold payment and a sheep only four-fold because the ox's work was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: Come and see how great the power of work is. For an ox, which the thief took away from its work, he pays five. For a sheep, which he did not take away from any work, he pays four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: why does the תורה make the payment for an ox (five) bigger than for a sheep (four)? רבי מאיר gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox plows and works, so stealing it also stops useful work from being done. A sheep does no work like that. The extra fifth payment reflects how important work is.

keyTerms.meaning: The power or importance of work
He stopped it from its work

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל מְלָאכָה:
phrases.english: Come and see how great the power of work is:
For an ox, which he took away from its work: five.
phrases.notes: The numbers refer to the תורה's payment for a thief who slaughters or sells what he stole (שמות 21:37).

phrases.english: For a sheep, which he did not take away from its work: four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the reason for the different payments for an ox and a sheep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ox brings five because the thief also caused the loss of its work; the sheep brings four because it does no such work.

steps.title: A sheep pays less because of human dignity
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי gives a different reason for the difference: the thief had to carry the sheep on his shoulder, which embarrassed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: Come and see how great human dignity is. For an ox, which walked on its own legs, the thief pays five. For a sheep, which he had to carry on his shoulder, he pays four.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives another reason why the payment for an ox is bigger than the payment for a sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי gives a different reason, based not on work but on human dignity. When a thief carries a sheep on his shoulder, he lowers himself, and the תורה takes that shame into account by making his payment smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: Human dignity, the honor of people
He carried it on his shoulder

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much the תורה cares about a person's dignity. Even a thief's embarrassment is taken into account.

phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כְּבוֹד הַבְּרִיּוֹת:
phrases.english: Come and see how great human dignity is:
For an ox, which walked on its own legs: five.
For a sheep, which he carried on his shoulder: four.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for five versus four: רבי מאיר says it is because of lost work, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says it is because of the thief's embarrassment.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כְּבוֹד הַבְּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason from רבי מאיר's for the same five versus four difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sheep brings only four because the thief embarrassed himself by carrying it on his shoulder.

steps.title: New משנה: where sheep and goats may be raised
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that small animals may not be raised in ארץ ישראל, but may be raised in סוריא and in the wilderness areas of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל. But one may raise them in סוריא, and in the wilderness areas of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a rule about where people are allowed to raise sheep and goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids raising small animals in ארץ ישראל. It then names two places where it is allowed: סוריא, and the wilderness areas inside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the opening of a new משנה
סוריא, a land next to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל;
phrases.english: One may not raise small animals in the Land of Israel;
but one may raise them in Syria,
and in the wilderness areas of the Land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, unconnected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising small animals is forbidden in ארץ ישראל, but allowed in סוריא and in the wilderness areas of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: No chickens in Jerusalem, and no chickens for priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids raising chickens in ירושלים because of קדשים, and forbids כהנים to raise chickens anywhere in ארץ ישראל because of their טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not raise chickens in ירושלים, because of the קדשים there. כהנים may not raise chickens anywhere in ארץ ישראל, because of the טהרות they keep.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of animals you may not raise. Now it talks about chickens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ban is not about damage to other people's property. It is about protecting holy and pure food from becoming impure. In ירושלים the concern is קדשים, which are found there. For כהנים the concern is their טהרות, such as תרומה, so their ban covers all of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Foods that must be kept ritually pure, like תְּרוּמָה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules. The ban in ירושלים applies to everyone. The ban for כהנים applies everywhere in ארץ ישראל, but only to כהנים.

phrases.english: One may not raise chickens in Jerusalem,
because of the sacrificial meat;
phrases.notes: Chickens peck through garbage and could carry something impure onto the holy meat.

phrases.english: and priests may not [raise chickens] in the Land of Israel,
phrases.notes: The words 'raise chickens' aren't written again here, but they carry over from the first line.

phrases.english: because of the pure foods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין תַּרְנְגוֹלִין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of forbidden animals, moving from small animals to chickens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No chickens in ירושלים because of קדשים. כהנים may not raise chickens anywhere in ארץ ישראל because of טהרות.

steps.title: No pigs anywhere, and dogs only on a chain
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids raising pigs in any place, and allows a dog only if it is chained.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not raise pigs anywhere. A person may not raise a dog unless it is tied with a chain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more animals to its list: pigs and dogs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pigs get the strongest ban of all. The words בכל מקום mean the ban applies everywhere, not just in ארץ ישראל. A dog is allowed, but only when chained so it cannot cause harm.

phrases.english: One may not raise pigs anywhere.
A person may not raise a dog,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה קָשׁוּר בְּשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת.
phrases.english: unless it is tied with a chain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין חֲזִירִין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden animals in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pigs are forbidden everywhere. A dog is allowed only if chained.

steps.title: Pigeon traps must be far from settled areas
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting traps for pigeons only at least thirty ריס away from a settled area.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not spread traps for pigeons unless they are thirty ריס away from a settled area.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a rule about setting traps for pigeons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern here is catching birds that belong to other people. A trap set near where people live could catch their pigeons. A distance of thirty ריס keeps the trap far from those birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A settled area where people live

phrases.english: One may not spread traps for pigeons,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה רָחוֹק מִן הַיִּשּׁוּב
phrases.english: unless it is far from a settled area
thirty ris.
phrases.notes: A ריס is a measure of distance. Thirty of them is far, so people's own pigeons won't get caught.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹרְסִין נִישּׁוּבִים לְיוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with a rule about trapping birds rather than raising animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pigeon traps may only be set at least thirty ריס from a settled area.

steps.title: A ברייתא on where small animals may be raised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: small animals are forbidden in ארץ ישראל but allowed in its forests, allowed even in settled parts of סוריא, and certainly allowed in חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: You may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל, but you may raise them in its forests. In סוריא you may raise them even in a settled area. In חוצה לארץ, it is obviously allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that adds details to the משנה's rule about small animals from Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed small animals in the wilderness and in סוריא. This ברייתא adds that forests in ארץ ישראל are also allowed. It also makes clear that in סוריא even settled areas are fine. It moves from strict to less strict: ארץ ישראל, then סוריא, then חוצה לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals, like sheep and goats
Syria, a land next to ארץ ישראל with some of its laws

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: One may not raise small animals in the Land of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְגַדְּלִין בָּחוֹרָשִׁין שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: but one may raise them in the forests of the Land of Israel.
In Syria, even in a settled area,
and needless to say, outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first rule of the משנה (Step 21) and adds details from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small animals are allowed in forests of ארץ ישראל, anywhere in סוריא, and certainly in חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: A second ברייתא names specific wilderness areas
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא allows raising small animals in the wilderness of יהודה and the wilderness on the border of עכו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: You may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל, but you may raise them in the wilderness of יהודה and in the wilderness on the border of עכו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. It names which wilderness areas the משנה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'wilderness areas.' This ברייתא names two real places: מדבר יהודה and the wilderness near עכו. These are empty areas where flocks will not graze in other people's fields.

phrases.english: Another [ברייתא] teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל;
phrases.english: One may not raise small animals in the Land of Israel;
but one may raise them in the wilderness of Judea,
and in the wilderness on the border of Akko.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא that adds more allowed places, this time naming specific wildernesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small animals may be raised in מדבר יהודה and the wilderness near עכו.

steps.title: Large animals were never forbidden, since the public could not keep such a decree
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא explains that large animals may be raised, because חכמים only make a גזירה that most of the public can keep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they said you may not raise small animals, you may raise large animals. This is because חכמים only make a גזירה on the public if most of the public can keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by saying large animals are allowed. It gives a general rule for why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might expect large animals to be banned too. The ברייתא says no, because people could not live without cattle for work and farming. So a ban would fail, and חכמים do not make a גזירה that most people cannot keep.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep it, to be able to live with it

steps.whatToRemember: Small animals are banned in settled parts of ארץ ישראל, but allowed in forests, wildernesses, סוריא, and חוצה לארץ. Large animals are allowed, because a גזירה is only made if most of the צבור can keep it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין גוזרין גזרה על הצבור אלא אם כן רוב צבור יכולין לעמוד בה' is a basic limit on rabbinic decrees. It shows up in many places in ש״ס.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say large animals are safe. It says a ban on them would be too hard for most people to keep.

phrases.english: And even though they said
one may not raise small animals,
one may raise large animals;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין גּוֹזְרִין גְּזֵרָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: because we do not impose a decree on the public

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רוֹב צִבּוּר יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בָּהּ.
phrases.english: unless most of the public is able to keep it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from where small animals are allowed to why large animals were never banned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large animals may be raised, because a גזירה is only made if most of the צבור can keep it.

steps.title: Why large animals were not included in the decree
steps.stepSummary: Small animals can be brought from חוצה לארץ when needed, but large animals cannot, so חכמים did not forbid large ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Small animals can be brought in from outside the land, but large animals cannot be brought in from outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes explaining why large animals may be raised in ארץ ישראל. It contrasts how easy it is to import small animals with how hard it is to import large ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said חכמים only make a גזירה that most of the public can keep. This line shows why a ban on large animals would fail that test. A small animal can be brought from abroad whenever one is needed. Large animals are needed all the time for work, and people cannot keep importing them, so the public could not live with such a ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Small domesticated animal, such as a sheep or goat
Large domesticated animal, such as an ox or cow

steps.whatToRemember: The ban covers only small animals. Large animals are needed constantly and cannot easily be imported, so banning them would be a גזירה the public could not keep.

phrases.english: Small animals, it is possible to bring
phrases.notes: This is the reason behind step 27: why large animals were left out of the ban.

phrases.english: from outside the land;
large animals, it is impossible to bring
from outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִיא מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical reason behind step 27's principle that a גזירה must be one the public can keep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large animals are permitted because they cannot easily be imported, while small animals can be.

steps.title: Keeping small animals for thirty days before a festival or a son's wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: Even though raising small animals is forbidden, a person may keep them for thirty days before a רגל or before his son's wedding feast. He may not keep the last one he bought for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they said one may not raise small animals, a person may still keep them for thirty days before a festival, and for thirty days before his son's wedding feast. But he must not keep the last one for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an allowance to the ban on small animals. They may be kept for a short time before times when a lot of meat is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not keeping a flock long-term. It is a short holding period before a רגל or a wedding feast, when many animals are needed for food. The closing condition limits the allowance: the last animal bought must not be kept for a full thirty days. The גמרא explains this condition in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps or holds onto (for a while)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the ban on raising small animals. It is a limited time window before a festival or a feast, and the ban stays in place otherwise.

phrases.english: And even though they said
one may not raise small animals,
nevertheless he may keep it
thirty days before a festival,
and thirty days before his son's wedding feast.
Provided that he does not keep
the last one for thirty days.
phrases.notes: "The last one" is the animal he bought last, right before the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the reason behind the ban to a limited allowance within it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small animals may be kept for thirty days before a רגל or a son's wedding feast, but the last one bought may not be kept for thirty days.

steps.title: Once the festival passes, the animal may not be kept any longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the last clause. Someone might think the animal may be kept a full thirty days from when it was bought. The ברייתא teaches that once the רגל has passed, he may not keep it anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that if the festival has passed, and thirty days have not yet gone by since he bought the animal, he may keep it until the thirty days are done. So the ברייתא teaches that we do not say he is allowed thirty days. Rather, once the festival has passed, he should not keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed its last clause about "the last one." It shows what mistake that clause prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea is that the allowance is a set thirty days counted from the day of purchase. The ברייתא corrects this: the allowance exists only because of the רגל. The thirty days are only the time before the festival. Once the festival is over, the reason is gone, so he must stop keeping the animal right away, even if fewer than thirty days have passed.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind to say (introduces a possible mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The thirty-day allowance depends on the festival. It is not a fixed thirty days from the purchase. Once the festival has passed, the animal may no longer be kept.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the allowance depends on its reason. When the need is gone, the permission ends.

phrases.english: For it could have entered your mind to say
that if the festival has passed for him,
and from when he bought it until now

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתִּי לָא מְלוֹ לֵיהּ תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין;
phrases.english: thirty days have not yet been completed for him,
we do not say: for thirty days
it is permitted for him to keep it;
rather, since the festival has passed for him,
he should not keep it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final clause of the ברייתא in step 29 by showing which mistaken assumption it rules out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The allowance is a fixed thirty days from the purchase, even after the festival has passed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The allowance ends as soon as the festival passes, whether or not thirty days have gone by.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the רגל has passed, the animal may not be kept, even if thirty days have not yet passed since it was bought.
